title: Why fewer moving parts fail less

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: The page contrasts `ComplexTransferService` with `SimpleTransferService`. Why can the simple version never deadlock?

options.text: It keeps both balances in `AtomicInteger` fields, so it takes no lock
options.says: The page's simple version keeps int balances and guards them with synchronized (lock).

options.text: It takes its two locks in one fixed order, so no cycle can form
options.says: The page's simple version has a single lock, and says there are no ordering issues.

options.text: It guards both balances with one lock, so no cycle can form
options.says: The page says deadlocks require at least two locks acquired in different orders.

questions.stem: Two threads call `start()` at the same moment on the page's `SimpleStateMachine`, which is `IDLE`. Per the page, what happens?

options.text: One call returns true, and the other call returns false
options.says: The page says if two threads transition simultaneously, one succeeds and the other gets false.

options.text: Both calls return true, and the state becomes RUNNING
options.says: compareAndSet changes the state only if it is still the expected IDLE, so only one call can succeed.

options.text: One call waits on a lock until the other call is done
options.says: The page says CAS is lock-free, so no thread waits on a lock.

concepts: When two threads race for one compareAndSet transition, exactly one succeeds and the other gets false, with no lock and no deadlock.
Deadlock needs at least two locks taken in different orders, so one lock (or none) removes the risk.
